nits: A target slotted into a shadow host (a light-DOM child shown through a <slot>) leaves the host's other shadow-root content exposed (probe: `slotted: header hidden= null`); the issue only covers shadow roots that enclose the target, so this is outside its stated scope.

The inert test sets HTMLElement.prototype.inert and deletes it only at the end of the test body; if an assertion fails first, the property leaks into later tests. Do the cleanup in try/finally or afterEach.

@react-aria/utils already has createShadowTreeWalker (used by FocusScope) for walking across shadow roots; walkShadowRoot builds its own recursion on document.createTreeWalker instead. It works, but reusing the helper would keep shadow traversal in one place.

The test 'does not hide anything inside a shadow root when shadow DOM is disabled' asserts that document.body itself gets aria-hidden, which locks in arguably undesirable flag-off behaviour as expected; the comment could say it is documenting existing behaviour rather than the desired one.
